as_told: Army helicopter pilots at Fort Hood, next to Killeen, Texas, practised with their infrared cameras by finding indoor marijuana grow houses in the Austin area. The grow lamps made the houses easy to see as hot spots. The pilots supposedly knew where the grow houses were.
lesson: Indoor marijuana grow houses give off so much heat that an infrared camera can pick them out.
what_happened: I found no record that Fort Hood pilots trained on grow houses. The earliest telling I found is a Hacker News comment of 7 August 2023, which itself calls the story an urban legend and says an Austin American-Statesman article reported it; I could not find that article. Thermal imaging did detect indoor grows elsewhere: in 1992 federal agents in Oregon used a thermal imager from a car to find heat from halide grow lamps, and in 2001 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled such a scan of a home a search that needs a warrant.

earliest_telling.quote: Urban legend (and an article in the Austin American-Statesman) says that the nearby army base in Killeen would train helicopter pilots by using the known (to them) grow houses in the Austin area because they were easily visible in their IR cameras.

lesson_verdict.why: A U.S. Supreme Court opinion records that a thermal imager scanned from a car showed the roof and wall of a house as hot, and agents then found more than 100 marijuana plants grown under halide lamps. This is one documented case; LED lamps, which run cooler, may make such scans less useful now.

source.what: Kyllo v. United States, 533 U.S. 27 (2001), opinion of the Court
source.quote: Agent Elliott concluded that petitioner was using halide lights to grow marijuana in his house, which indeed he was.

search_steps: Open Library full-text search for "Fort Hood" helicopter "grow houses": 5 hits (all 1999-2012), none about the story.

Web searches (several wordings: Fort Hood, Killeen, Apache, Kiowa, FLIR, thermal, grow houses, Austin American-Statesman, Austin Chronicle, JTF-6): no news report of Fort Hood pilots training on grow houses.

Hacker News search (hn.algolia.com) for 'Killeen grow houses', 'army base grow houses helicopter', 'Fort Hood FLIR', 'Fort Hood marijuana' and others: one relevant comment, dylan604, 2023-08-07, item 37037821. Saved.

Tried to find the Austin American-Statesman article that the comment names: not found by web search. One request to the statesman.com site search returned only a script challenge page, so I could not search the paper's own archive.
Read the replies under the comment in the saved page: four replies argue about whether cars swamp the heat signal; none gives the article or corrects the claim.

Austin Chronicle 'Naked City' (2001-05-25) and 'When Weed Is Really Weed' (2003-01-10): a Department of Public Safety helicopter and the Capital Area Narcotics Task Force raided a Spicewood property in May 2001 over plants that were ragweed. Police helicopter, not Army; not saved because not quoted.

Texas Observer 'Death From Above': refused (403). rave.ca copy of a 2008 Houston Chronicle story on Fort Hood Kiowa helicopters helping the Border Patrol at Laredo: connection failed. NORTHCOM article on a Fort Hood aviation unit on the border (2008): refused (403). These show Fort Hood helicopters supported law enforcement on the border, not in Austin.
Reddit search API: refused (403). Google Groups search: page loads results by script only, so no results could be read.
English Wikipedia search API for Killeen grow houses helicopter: no article on the story (top hit is the Fort Hood article, not about this).
Google Books API returned 429 and HathiTrust returned 403. Free newspaper archives were not searched, because they do not cover recent Texas papers.
Lesson source: Kyllo v. United States (2001), Supreme Court opinion at law.cornell.edu. Saved.
confidence_note: The only telling I found is a 2023 forum comment that already calls the story an urban legend. The Statesman article it names may exist in the paper's paid archive; if it does, it could be an earlier telling or a record of the event. I did not find a record that rules it out.
